learningObjectives.title: The problem of evil and suffering

questions.q: What does the aim of punishment called 'retribution' mean?
options: The criminal deserves to be punished and should pay for what they have done
The criminal should be helped to change their behaviour
The public should be protected from the criminal
Other people should be put off committing the same crime
questions.explain: Retribution is the idea that wrongdoers deserve to suffer a punishment proportionate to their crime, reflecting 'an eye for an eye'.

questions.q: The teaching 'an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth' comes from which book of the Bible?
questions.explain: This principle of proportionate retribution is found in Exodus 21:24.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the four main aims of punishment?
questions.explain: The four recognised aims are deterrence, protection, retribution and reformation; revenge is not one of them.

questions.q: Which aim of punishment focuses on changing a criminal's behaviour so they do not reoffend?
questions.explain: Reformation aims to rehabilitate offenders so they can return to society as law-abiding citizens.

questions.q: What is the aim of 'deterrence' as a purpose of punishment?
options: To keep the public safe from dangerous offenders
To put people off committing crimes through fear of punishment
To make the criminal suffer for what they did
To help the criminal learn a new skill
questions.explain: Deterrence uses the threat of punishment to discourage the offender and others from committing crime.

questions.q: Which statement best describes the aim of 'protection' in punishment?
options: Making the criminal feel guilty about their actions
Ensuring the criminal is treated with dignity
Keeping society safe by preventing the criminal from harming others
Teaching the criminal a moral lesson
questions.explain: Protection safeguards the public, for example by imprisoning dangerous offenders so they cannot commit further crimes.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a crime against property?
questions.explain: Theft is a crime against property, whereas murder, assault and kidnapping are crimes against the person.

questions.q: A judge sentences a violent offender to a long prison term mainly to keep the public safe. Which aim of punishment is this?
questions.explain: Removing a dangerous offender from society to prevent further harm reflects the aim of protection.

questions.q: A Christian argues against the death penalty. Which belief is most likely to support their view?
options: Criminals deserve to be punished harshly
Life is sacred and only God has the right to take it
An eye for an eye is the fairest response
questions.explain: The sanctity of life teaches that human life is God-given and should not be taken by humans, so many Christians oppose capital punishment.

questions.q: When Peter asked how many times he should forgive someone, what did Jesus reply?
questions.explain: In Matthew 18:22 Jesus says 'seventy-seven times' (rendered 'seventy times seven' in some translations), meaning forgiveness should have no limit.

questions.q: Which parable of Jesus teaches about the importance of forgiving others?
questions.explain: In the Parable of the Unforgiving (Unmerciful) Servant, a man forgiven a huge debt is condemned for refusing to forgive a small one.

questions.q: Jesus said 'Let any one of you who is without sin be the first to throw a stone.' What does this teach?
options: Sinners should always be punished by stoning
People should not judge others harshly and should show mercy
Only religious leaders may forgive sins
questions.explain: Spoken to the crowd about the woman caught in adultery (John 8), it teaches humility, mercy and not condemning others.

questions.q: What does Jesus' teaching 'Love your enemies' in the Sermon on the Mount encourage believers to do?
options: Seek revenge on those who harm them
Avoid all people who have wronged them
Show love and forgiveness even to those who wrong them
Punish enemies before they can cause harm
questions.explain: In Matthew 5:44 Jesus calls believers to love and pray for their enemies rather than seek retaliation.

questions.q: A Christian whose relative was badly hurt in an attack chooses to forgive the attacker. Which teaching most directly supports this choice?
options: 'An eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth'
questions.explain: Jesus taught that forgiving others is central to Christian discipleship, and that God forgives those who forgive others.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of natural evil?
questions.explain: Natural evil is suffering caused by nature, such as earthquakes, floods and disease, rather than by human choices.

questions.q: How is 'moral evil' best defined?
options: Suffering caused by the actions and choices of human beings
Suffering that has no cause at all
questions.explain: Moral evil results from human free choices, such as violence, cruelty and war.

questions.q: The 'inconsistent triad', associated with Epicurus, states that it is hard to believe all three of the following at once. Which three?
options: God is all-powerful, all-loving, yet evil and suffering exist
God is distant, unknowable, yet good
Humans are sinful, free, and powerless
Evil is an illusion, real, and necessary
questions.explain: The problem of evil questions how an omnipotent, omnibenevolent God can coexist with the reality of evil and suffering.

questions.q: In the Bible, Job is best described as which of the following?
options: A king punished for his pride
A man who kept his faith in God despite great suffering
questions.explain: The Book of Job explores undeserved suffering, with Job remaining faithful even after losing his family, health and wealth.

questions.q: What is the main idea of the 'free will' response to the problem of evil?
options: God causes evil to test believers
God gave humans free will, and moral evil results from humans choosing to do wrong
Suffering is always a punishment for sin
questions.explain: The free will defence argues that genuine freedom to choose good must also allow the possibility of choosing evil.

questions.q: A church responds to a natural disaster by running collections and a food bank for the victims. This is an example of a religious response to suffering through:
questions.explain: Many believers respond to suffering practically through charity, following teachings to love and care for those in need.
